forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. No publicly confirmed held negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals occurred before EOD 2026-06-16. The June 11-12 Qatari mediator work in Tehran was indirect technical gap-narrowing with no named US principal present. The Islamabad Memorandum was signed electronically/remotely by Presidents Trump and Pezeshkian on June 17 — one day after the horizon — and the Lake Lucerne (Bürgenstock) four-party convened session occurred June 21. No official Iranian statement rescinding the June 1 suspension was issued before June 16. The agreed-text milestone on June 12 involved Pakistani PM confirmation and Qatari mediation, not a convened US-Iran session.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

On June 21, 2026, a four-party high-level session convened at the Bürgenstock hotel complex overlooking Lake Lucerne, Switzerland, with named US principals (Witkoff-led delegation), named Iranian principals (Araghchi-led delegation), hosted by named mediators Pakistan and Qatar. Mediators' joint readout confirmed agreement on a 'road map towards reaching a final deal within 60 days' and establishment of a High Level Committee with working groups on nuclear, sanctions, and monitoring.

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. No TIER1-confirmed direct bilateral Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both directions) within any rolling 48h window between June 10-24 was confirmed. June 14: IDF struck Beirut, but US intervention prevented Iranian retaliation from taking place. June 20: Iran declared Hormuz re-closed citing Israeli strikes in Lebanon but no confirmed Iranian strikes on Israeli territory occurred. The June 7-8 exchange (pre-window) was the last bilateral exchange. The major US-Iran exchange (June 27-28: US strikes five Iranian coastal sites, Iran strikes Kuwait and Bahrain US bases) is outside the June 10-24 window. Proxy-only actions (Hezbollah) did not qualify per ambiguity rule.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE from 0.20 to 0.08. Peak single-day transit of ~49 AIS-visible vessels recorded June 24 (the highest of the conflict), supported by the IMO corridor and Oman's six authorized waypoints. However, June 25: IRGC ordered vessels in the southern corridor to turn back, struck Singapore-flagged EVER LOVELY, and the IMO temporarily paused its evacuation initiative. Daily transits fell back to 43 June 25 and are now disrupted. A 7-day rolling average of 50/day by July 2 would require sustained daily counts well above 50 through July 2 — implausible given the June 25 IRGC crackdown and ongoing corridor uncertainty. With 2 days to resolution, this forecast is near-NO. IRGC cargo-ship strike June 25 also re-triggered insurer risk reassessment.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE from 0.30 to 0.25. US CENTCOM issued a press release announcing 'mine clearance mission' commencement with Arleigh Burke destroyers and UUV assets in Hormuz (April 2026). However, search results as of late June confirm large-scale mine clearance has not yet begun at scale. The June 25 IRGC cargo-ship strike and IRGC corridor crackdown have disrupted the preconditions for demining (safe operating environment). Iran reportedly lost track of some planted mines, adding complexity. The Islamabad MOU and Lake Lucerne talks created a deconfliction cell for Hormuz, but active mine clearance requires sustained ceasefire adherence. Chatham House June 2026 analysis: 'large-scale clearance has yet to begin.' With 10 days remaining, limited scope operations may be announced but full commencement per criteria is less probable than originally assessed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE from 0.45 to 0.55. Multiple sources confirm that without ultra-Orthodox (UTJ) support, the Knesset is expected to dissolve automatically by July 17 — making second/third readings before July 15 more urgent and probable. UTJ exited the government in July 2025 (leaving coalition at 60 seats); Shas remains but under pressure. The coalition advanced the bill specifically to control the dissolution timing. However, the bill still lacks a fixed election date — it specifies a Sept 8–Oct 20 window with the date to be inserted before final readings. Netanyahu wants October; haredim want September before High Holy Days. The date dispute could delay final readings past July 15. Raised from 0.45 to 0.55 on the auto-dissolution pressure creating urgency for the coalition to complete the readings before July 17.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE from 0.35 to 0.60. Substantial developments in the 20-day catch-up window. UTJ exited the government in July 2025, leaving the coalition at 60 seats (bare majority). The coalition is now actively pursuing a managed self-dissolution via the Knesset dissolution bill (first reading 106-0 on June 2). Auto-dissolution is expected by July 17 without ultra-Orthodox support for final readings. If the dissolution bill passes final reading before Oct 27 — which sources describe as likely — that constitutes 'dissolve early' per resolution criteria. Shas remains but under pressure. Election is expected between Sept 8 and Oct 20, which is before Oct 27. Even a controlled dissolution before Oct 27 satisfies the YES criterion. Raised substantially from 0.35 to 0.60 reflecting the near-certain trajectory toward pre-Oct-27 dissolution via managed path.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Coalition formally advancing a dissolution bill that passes final reading counts as dissolve early = YES.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran conclude a final binding agreement (beyond the Islamabad MOU framework) before EOD 2026-08-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. The Islamabad MOU (June 17) created a 60-day ceasefire extension with working groups on nuclear, sanctions, and Hormuz. The 60-day clock runs to approximately August 16-17. Core unresolved issues remain: Iran's HEU stockpile disposition, enrichment levels, ballistic missile program (explicitly excluded from MOU), and verification protocols. Vance stated Iran agreed to allow IAEA inspections to resume. The US-Iran June 27-28 exchange (US strikes five coastal sites, Iran strikes Kuwait/Bahrain US bases) then a new ceasefire agreement for Qatar talks on June 29 shows the track is volatile. A final binding agreement within 48 days is historically improbable given the gap between the MOU framework and a verifiable nuclear accord. Base rate for converting ceasefire MOUs to final agreements within 60 days in comparable cases is low.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US and Iran sign or formally announce a comprehensive final agreement (not merely an extension of the MOU) that resolves Iran's nuclear program disposition and is confirmed by both State Dept and Iranian MFA before EOD 2026-08-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/Axios) plus official State Dept or Iran MFA statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A further MOU extension or another framework document without final nuclear-program resolution = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A partial deal covering only Hormuz or sanctions without the nuclear component = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will an IRGC-attributed interdiction of a commercial vessel in or near Hormuz cause a formal suspension of the IMO-coordinated transit corridor before EOD 2026-07-14?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. On June 25, the IRGC struck Singapore-flagged EVER LOVELY, prompting the IMO to temporarily pause its evacuation initiative. The IRGC also ordered vessels in the southern corridor to turn back. As of June 30, the IMO pause is in effect. The question is whether a further IRGC interdiction will cause the corridor to be formally suspended (not merely paused) within the next 14 days. The June 27-28 US-Iran strikes and the June 29 agreed Qatar talks create a fragile but extant ceasefire dynamic. IRGC has demonstrated willingness to act against vessels despite the MOU. Base rate for a further incident within 14 days given the June 25 precedent and ongoing corridor tension is elevated.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports that a second (post-June 25) IRGC-attributed strike or seizure of a commercial vessel in the Hormuz/Gulf of Oman area occurs between 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-14 AND the IMO or a major flag-state formally suspends (not merely pauses) the coordinated transit corridor as a result.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg TIER1 for the strike; IMO or UK MARITME TRADE OPERATIONS (UKMTO) statement for the formal suspension.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A temporary IMO pause without a formal suspension announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. An IRGC warning or vessel turning-back without confirmed strike or seizure = NO.
